newsitem.title: USA: European Union and KEDO reach agreement.
newsitem.headline: European Union and KEDO reach agreement.

text.p: The European Union has agreed to join the international consortium working with North Korea to dismantle the communist state's nuclear programme, a spokesman for the consortium said on Thursday.

He said the Korean Peninsula Development Organisation (KEDO) and the Commission of European Communities have initialed an agreement for the European Atomic Energy Community (EURATOM) to become an executive board member.

The United States, Japan and South Korea are currently the other executive board members and leaders of the consortium that was established following an agreement signed in Geneva in 1994 between Washington and Pyongyang.
The 15-country European Union's membership of KEDO had been expected for some months. It was first announced in March by KEDO's executive director, Stephen Bosworth, a former U.S. ambassador.

"EURATOM's accession to KEDO sends a very important signal of support for KEDO's mission and efforts in North Korea," the spokesman for the New York-based KEDO said. "Its financial contribution will also help KEDO meet its various obligations."
He said the European Union had agreed to provide 75 million ECUs ($86.29 million) to the project over five years.

Under the $4.5 billion Geneva agreement, Washington promised the isolationist state two light-water reactors generating 1,000 megawatts of power each. The reactors have been promised by approximately 2003, if Pyongyang freezes and ultimately dismantles its existing nuclear programme. North Korea was assured interim energy in the form of 500,000 metric tons of heavy fuel per year for heating and electricity.
Light-water reactors are less suitable for producing weapons-grade plutonium than the graphite-moderated reactors built by North Korea.

The new membership agreement, reached on May 15 but not announced until Thursday, would be sent to KEDO's executive board and the European Union Council of Ministers for formal approval, the spokesman said. General members of KEDO are Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Indonesia, Finland, Argentina and Chile.
